title: Salary Packaging NT: Turning Your Hourly Rate into Annual, Fortnightly & Super
description: Use our hourly to annual calculator for a 38-hour week, fortnightly pay, tax, and super. Includes salary packaging NT considerations for Northern Territory workers.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary in Australia?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, so annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. This gives a base figure before tax, super, or any salary packaging. Remember that award rates, casual loading, and overtime can change the calculation.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. It compensates for entitlements like paid leave that casuals don't receive. If you are a casual, your effective hourly rate becomes the base rate plus 25%. Our calculator has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically – never enter a rate that already includes it.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my pay?
faqs.a: The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For 2026–27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution. If you are considering salary packaging NT, note that packaging arrangements can affect your super base, but this estimate shows your standard super before any packaging.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia

If you earn an hourly wage or have a salary offer, understanding your annual, fortnightly, and superannuation figures helps you compare jobs and budget. This guide explains the standard conversion for a 38-hour week, the role of the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and super – all with Australian tax rules.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

Annual gross pay (before tax and super) is calculated as:

**hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a standard full-time week of 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00:

- Weekly gross = $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Fortnightly gross = $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00
- Annual gross = $1,140.00 × 52 = $59,280.00

This formula works for any hourly rate. If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The calculator on [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your exact hours.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive an extra 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Many workers are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for specific industries and roles.

### Casual Loading: What It Means

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate typically includes a 25% loading to compensate for not receiving paid leave. Our calculator has a checkbox to add casual loading on top of your base rate. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – always start with the base award or minimum rate. For more details, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 for 2026–27). Super is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. For the example above ($59,280 annual gross), the super contribution would be $7,113.60 per year. This is an estimate; actual super may vary if you have salary sacrifice arrangements. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page shows how these apply.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian workers are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly gross by 2. Using the $30/hour example:

- Fortnightly gross = $1,140 × 2 = $2,280
- After tax and Medicare (estimated), your fortnightly net might be around $1,850–$1,950 depending on your total income.

### Salary Packaging NT Considerations

If you live or work in the Northern Territory, salary packaging (also called salary sacrifice) is common, especially in not-for-profit and public sector roles. Salary packaging allows you to pay for certain expenses (like a car or rent) with pre-tax dollars, reducing your taxable income. However, this calculator does **not** include salary packaging deductions. The figures shown are your base pay before any packaging arrangements. If you are considering **salary packaging NT**, use this estimate to see your gross pay, then consult a tax professional for the impact on your net income.

### Average Earnings in the Northern Territory

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in the Northern Territory were $1,984.10 per week. This is an average across all industries and occupations – it is **not** the median for any specific job. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) reference for more context.

### Important Notes and Limitations

This conversion assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a personalised calculation, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your hourly rate. You can also explore our [reference tables](/data) for more benchmarks.
